A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Semi-knockoffs study. The main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–F are readable and matchable across pagination changes and the added experiment.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix F report original simulations and Wisconsin Diagnostic Breast Cancer experiments, including power, error control, discoveries and computational results.

after.justification: The original empirical results are retained, with an additional high-dimensional simulation in Appendix F.5.3 and Figure 25.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–4 and the two-imputer residual-permutation procedure are unchanged. Calling derandomization Rao–Blackwellization explains an existing procedure; testing ten permutations adds a parameter setting rather than a method component.

E1.justification: Appendix F.5.3 adds an underdetermined synthetic feature-selection scenario with p=400 exceeding n=300 and randomly located Gaussian signal coefficients. The earlier Gaussian, heavy-tailed, masked-correlation and breast-cancer settings remain.

E2.justification: Existing comparisons retain their baselines. The new high-dimensional experiment reuses Knockoff, dCRT and HRT from the earlier FDR comparisons. SKO_p10 is another permutation setting of the proposed method, not a new baseline.

E3.justification: The added experiment uses n=300, p=400, Lasso for both learner and imputer, and includes a ten-permutation SKO setting. Section 5 also newly reports evaluations at n=100, 200 and 400. Protocols for the retained experiments are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix F.5.3 adds a stress test of error control when high dimensionality makes conditional estimation difficult, including comparisons of one, five and ten permutations. Section 5 adds a brief qualitative sample-size sensitivity finding. Earlier robustness and double-robustness analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the statement that experiments are repeated 50 times and the same distributional reporting practices. The added boxplots introduce no new uncertainty-estimation procedure, seed disclosure, confidence intervals or significance analysis.

E6.justification: New Figure 25 reports power, FDP and AUC distributions, with predictive R² of 0.874 with splitting and 0.963 without splitting. It shows elevated FDP for Knockoff and dCRT and increasing SKO power with derandomization. Section 5 adds qualitative smaller-sample findings; matched earlier results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 4.3 replaces the assertion that similar estimated samplers yield i.i.d. observations with independent sampling from distributions that converge. This locally revises the mathematical reasoning. The formal theorems, assumptions and Appendix E proofs are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and discussion retain the same claims about model-agnostic testing without sample splitting, oracle error guarantees, stability and double robustness. The added experiments support existing claims rather than redefine the contribution.

C2.justification: New Appendix F.5.3 attributes dCRT and knockoff failures to inaccurate sampling in high dimensions and tentatively links the loss-based methods' robustness to double robustness. Existing limitations concerning simple response-conditioned imputers remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Figure 25 and Appendix F.5.3 document the added simulation's covariance, sparsity, coefficient and noise distributions, and Lasso learner/imputer choices. These provide reproducibility information for the new experiment; existing software and code-access disclosures are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work discussion and novelty positioning are retained. Appendix F.5.3 reuses Blain et al. (2025) to illustrate the existing concern about knockoff validity. Bibliographic URL trimming does not change research positioning.

P1.justification: There are localized explanatory edits in Sections 4–5, an added Appendix F.5.3, and new acknowledgements. Title capitalization, affiliation and publication information are updated. The overall narrative and section organization remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 adds the three-panel Figure 25, adjusts main-text figure placement and corrects a missing tilde in Figure 2. Earlier real-data Figures 25–27 become Figures 26–28 and move across pages; their plotted results and the existing tables are retained.

improvement.justification: Appendix F.5.3 and Figure 25 provide useful direct evidence in a p>n setting absent from v1's FDR benchmarks, with a documented simulation setup. This modestly strengthens empirical support. The gain remains limited: guarantees with estimated imputers are still conjectural, and the additional sample-size findings receive only a brief qualitative report.
